text:
anita: heads-up — we saw a tenant with mixed tiny chat queries + periodic 100MB embedding batches starve the continuous batcher today. latency spikes for small requests jumped to 1.2s.
josh: ugh. is this the same tenant that has aggressive prefetch turned on? or just huge payloads interleaving?
maria: payload size + long KV cache warms. embeddings come in bursts, they fill microbatches and delay window close for everyone.
elliot: can you paste the request traces? curious if it's head-of-line blocking inside the coalescer or admission not applying backpressure.
sam: logs: ```
[2026-03-21T14:02:12.123Z] tenant=acme embed_batch size=96 tokens=2k enqueue_time=0.3ms
[2026-03-21T14:02:12.125Z] tenant=acme small_req id=xyz enqueue_time=1.1ms wait=850ms served
```
sam: also repro script: `wrk -c 50 -t 5 -d 30s --script small-vs-large.lua` (will attach later)
anita: TL;DR — long requests are monopolizing batch windows. We need a short-term mitigation + long-term interface change.
josh: short term: enforce a per-tenant microwindow cap for large-payload ops. e.g., if a tenant has >X outstanding tokens, steer the next embeds to a dedicated lane or degrade to lower-parallelism model.
maria: we tried dedicated lanes before; problem was fragmentation and wasted GPU fills during low load. but for bursty tenants it could help.
elliot: another option: burst-gating — allow a burst token budget that decays. When budget exhausted, future large requests are either queued in slow lane or get an earlier fallback. Similar to token buckets.
anita: i like burst-gating. question: where do we keep the budget state? per-scheduler instance or centralized? soon-to-be-sharded schedulers complicate centralized counters.
josh: per-instance with consistent hashing of tenant -> scheduler shard is simpler and avoids cross-shard locks. downside: uneven bursts across shards.
maria: also need to expose metrics so SRE can tune the cap: `burst_budget_consumed`, `burst_rejects`, `fastpath_fills`. ops-bot: added metric requests as a follow-up.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: metric ticket created: INF-5423
elliot: interface-wise, we should add a small enum on the request envelope: `preferred_lane: fast|balanced|bulk` (optional). that lets clients hint, and internal policy rewrites it for fairness.
anita: agree. clients can hint but runtime enforces. also add a `max_wait_ms` hint so small chat clients can opt-out of bulk waits.
sam: implementation sketch: when enqueueing:
```
if payload.size > LARGE_THRESHOLD:
  if burst_budget[tenant] <= 0:
    route -> slow_lane
  else:
    deduct(burst_budget, payload.size)
    route -> bulk_lane
```
sam: need recovery path — budget should replenish over time (exponential decay) and also be refillable by ops for troubleshooting.
josh: tradeoffs: slow_lane adds predictable latency but reduces head-of-line. Bulk_lane keeps throughput. We must ensure GPU packing still gets decent utilization — add opportunistic packer that steals slack from fast lane when bulk_lane is starved.
maria: important: KV cache interactions. If we shove embeds to bulk_lane with cold KV, latency will still be high and can still stall overall memory pressure. Maybe prefetch should be deprioritized for bulk_lane unless explicitly requested.
elliot: and consider admission signals back to clients (429 with Retry-After) vs server-side reroute. For PLG developers, silent reroute is less surprising but may break latency SLAs.
anita: short-term plan: 1) add burst_budget per-tenant (per-shard) 2) introduce `preferred_lane` hint and runtime rewrite 3) create slow_lane that guarantees fastpath tail isolation 4) add observability dashboards. target: canary in 2 weeks.
josh: long-term: rethink batching API so tenants can declaratively register workload classes (chat/embedding/streaming) and have dedicated soft quotas.
maria: also propose an RFC for cache-aware admission — admission should consider KV hit rates and not just token counts.
elliot: I'll draft the RFC for the `preferred_lane` envelope + burst budget semantics. will include failure modes (split-brain budget drift) and refill algorithms.
anita: thanks. please include a small sim we can run to show utilization vs tail-latency under different budgets.
sam: I can build the sim (simplified event-driven) and link in the RFC.
anita: awesome. if anyone sees this pattern in other tenants, drop a note here with tenant id + sample logs.
josh: fwiw I've add a quick flag `--prefer-fast-lane-for-small` in the local dev runtime to help test.
maria: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy to canary started for flag `burst-gating` (canary=3 nodes)
